paraphrase: The scripture opens with the fivefold salutation: homage to the Arhats, to the Siddhas, to the Ācāryas, to the Upādhyāyas, to all the Sādhus in the world.

original.text: ṇamo arihaṃtāṇaṃ, ṇamo siddhāṇaṃ, ṇamo āiriyāṇaṃ, ṇamo uvajjhāyāṇaṃ, ṇamo loe savvasāhūṇaṃ
original.edition: from memory (skeleton); wording to be checked against a critical edition

notes: The Dhavalā discusses whether this maṅgala was composed by Puṣpadanta himself or taken up from tradition.

paraphrase: Souls are to be investigated through fourteen 'ways of search' (mārgaṇā): destiny, sense-faculty, body-type, activity, sex, passion, knowledge, restraint, perception, soul-colour, capacity for liberation, right faith, rationality and intake of nourishment.

Of human females who have completed their development, the sūtra states in which of the stages of quality (guṇasthāna) they are found; the manuscripts' reading of whether the word 'restrained' (saṃjada) occurs here — and so whether women reach the stages of full renunciation and beyond — became the subject of a 20th-century Digambara controversy; the Dhavalā explains the passage as concerning psychological sex (bhāva-veda).
notes: Low confidence on the sūtra number and on details; recorded as a known controversy (recent).
